_comment: TWO jobs, TWO dedicated binaries. (1) THE BLUE-REPORT LOCKDOWN. report.md is read-only to every seat EXCEPT the allowlisted author agent_type (frank-exchange-of-views:blue-synthesizer); a response seat changes it only through `feov-record blue edit`. PreToolUse DENIES a non-author raw write (Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit by file_path, or a Bash cp/mv/tee/redirect/sed -i into blue/report.md) WHEN THAT PATH IS INSIDE A LIVE RUN; outside a run it is a no-op, which is what it was always documented to be and was not. PostToolUse BLOCKS and forces a repair if a non-author call dropped a finding-marker by any mechanism (the exotic-Bash backstop the PreToolUse verb-set cannot enumerate). The gate reads agent_type from the hook stdin (present inside subagent tool calls) and decides in-binary. (2) RUN AND IDENTITY INJECTION (#281, #510): when the call is NOT denied and the payload cwd resolves a live-run marker, PreToolUse REWRITES EVERY Bash command in that run, prefixing `export FEOV_RUN='<runDir>'; export FEOV_AGENT_ID='<agent>'; export FEOV_AGENT_TYPE='<type>'; ` — so a seat stops typing an absolute path it can mistype (measured: one typo cost five manifest receipts and produced a false bug report), and never loses the identity that binds it to its seat on the record. The TYPE is a different fact from the handle and refuses a different thing: agent_id says which agent, agent_type says which configuration it was dispatched as, so `register` can reject a seat id from the wrong family — the membership half the roster gate states outright that it cannot reach. UNCONDITIONAL, WITH NO MATCHER, and that is the correction: injection was gated on recognising `feov-record` in command position, a pattern standing in for a schema whose miss was silent — no injection, no error, and a seat's identity simply absent, which reads exactly like a main-session call. The shape was widened three times, each after a run had already paid (a heredoc bail cost one seat its bibliography, command substitution cost another its identity, and `RB="…/feov-record"; $RB …` — a seat aliasing the long path, which no command-text matcher can see — cost 21 of 65 registers across six runs their agent_id). The harm the matcher claimed to prevent cannot occur: injection PREPENDS, so a documentation write or a friction message carrying the token is byte-identical either way. A needless `export` on a command that does not use the tool is inert; a missing one destroys a seat's work. Deny wins structurally: hookgate.PreOutcome consults the deny arm first and cannot return a rewrite once it fires, because the protocol permits ONE hookSpecificOutput document and a rewrite emitted in a deny's place is a lockdown that silently opened. THE MATCHER IS WIDE AND THE DECISION IS NARROW, because Claude Code matches on TOOL NAME and there is no path predicate at the matcher layer. That trade is only safe while the binary cannot fail, which is why these are DEDICATED SINGLE-PURPOSE BINARIES rather than verbs on feov-record: as `feov-record hook pretooluse` the invocation carried no --seat-id, the identity-scoped surface refused it, and the refusal's exit 2 denied every mutating tool call in the session. The bootstrap guard mirrors prosthetic-conscience: a fresh plugin-cache version ships without binaries (they arrive via doctor --fix), and an unguarded hook would crash-storm every tool call in that window; the guard degrades to ONE stderr line. The decision ALWAYS travels in the stdout JSON with exit 0, enforced at the process boundary by hookcmd.Run rather than documented on a leaf.

hooks.command: B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/feov-pretooluse"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B"; fi; echo 'frank-exchange-of-views: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/feov-posttooluse"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B"; fi; echo 'frank-exchange-of-views: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2
